articles.title_zh: China Gas doubles 20-year Venture Global LNG deal to 1 MMtpy
articles.content_orig:
China Gas doubled its 20-year LNG deal with U.S. exporter Venture Global to 1 MMtpy from 0.5 MMtpy, with Louisiana deliveries starting as early as 2030.
(P&GJ) — China Gas Holdings doubled the annual volume of a 20-year LNG supply deal with U.S. exporter Venture Global to 1 MMtpy, the Chinese company said Nov. 18, according to Reuters.
Subsidiaries of the two companies signed the agreement at the APEC CEO Summit, replacing a deal signed in September for 0.5 MMtpy. Deliveries are expected to begin as early as 2030.
The agreement expands China Gas' total contracted long-term LNG portfolio to 4 MMtpy, the company said.
"This agreement closely connects reliable gas supplies with a growing market. It not only provides solid support for China Gas to implement its global LNG trading strategy but also further deepens practical cooperation in energy trade between Chinese and US companies," said Minghui Liu, chairman and president of China Gas.
Venture Global CEO Mike Sabel said the company would supply reliable, low-cost U.S. LNG from its Louisiana projects to meet China's growing energy demand.
China halted imports of U.S. LNG in March 2025 after Beijing imposed tariffs on U.S. energy products.

articles.title_orig: Trump arrives in China ahead of high-stakes talks with Xi, Putin amid US technical outages
articles.title_zh: Trump arrives in China ahead of high-stakes talks with Xi, Putin amid US technical outages
articles.content_orig:
Watch: BBC correspondents discuss historic Trump, Xi and Putin meeting
Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin met for the first time in more than a year on Wednesday, as they prepared for landmark talks in China with Xi Jinping.
The US president was greeted off his plane by the Chinese leader as he arrived in Shenzhen for a summit of Asia-Pacific leaders, which will culminate in a closely-watched meeting between the pair and the Russian president.
After a carefully choreographed handshake and hug between Trump and Xi on the tarmac, the US president later greeted and exchanged pleasantries with Putin ahead of a reception.
Trump and Putin are expected to hold one-on-one talks on the sidelines of the summit on Thursday, in which the war in Ukraine could be discussed.
However the main focus during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum (Apec) will be on the US-China-Russia talks on Thursday - the first time the trio of leaders have met together in person.
A full agenda has not been made public but there have been various hints about what could be discussed, including the wars in Ukraine and Iran, nuclear proliferation, trade tensions and developments in artificial intelligence.
After a warm reception from Xi, the leaders of the US and Russia shook hands ahead of a reception
It was not clear on Wednesday what form separate Trump-Putin talks would take, though a Kremlin spokesperson indicated short informal talks may happen without large delegations in the room.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has raised fears of a plan to end the war being discussed in the absence of representatives from Kyiv or Europe.
Wednesday's handshake was the first in-person meeting between Trump and Putin since August 2025, when the Russian leader travelled to Alaska for talks on the Ukraine war which failed to deliver a breakthrough.
Xi's personal reception for Trump at the airport mimicked a similar move by the US president when the Chinese leader visited Washington in September, a gesture Xi described as "special".
In Shenzhen, a red carpet was rolled out in front of Air Force One for Trump, with a cheering crowd, honour guard, military flyover and flowers presentation all in place to welcome him.
Chinese state-run news agency Xinhua quoted Xi as saying he wanted to pursue a "constructive strategic and stable relationship based on respect, fairness, and equality".
Xi's greeting will be seen as a diplomatic gesture designed to begin the week's talks with his American counterpart on a cordial note.
A lavish welcome ceremony was laid on for Trump's arrival
The south-east Chinese city the Apec summit is being held in is a booming area for manufacturing and advanced tech.
It comes against the backdrop of the ousting of Nvidia chief executing Jensen Huang, who admitted to having an affair with a woman suspected by US intelligence of spying for Beijing - a claim dismissed as a "smear" by China.
Trump has pursued warmer relations with China but the incident points to ongoing tensions between the two powers.
Several hours before Trump's arrival, Putin landed in Shenzhen and held around two hours of talks with Xi, with whom he has pressed for closer economic and defence relations.
Xi said both countries would "move forward steadily and boldly" and that the relationship was "stable as a mountain, unshaken by storms".

articles.content_orig:
President Donald Trump warned Iran on Monday that it would face unprecedented retaliation if it were to carry out an attack on Washington, D.C.
Iran launched drone attacks against Kuwait Tuesday night after U.S. forces struck an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) missile launch site on Qeshm Island earlier, officials said.
Kuwait's military said its air defenses were intercepting drones, while neighboring Bahrain also warned of a potential threat and urged residents to seek safety.
"Kuwaiti air defenses are currently countering hostile drone attacks," the Kuwaiti army said in a statement, without providing further details.
The army's general staff also said any explosions heard were the result of "air defense systems intercepting hostile attacks."
ARMY IDS 2 VICTIMS KILLED IN JORDAN AIR BASE ATTACK; TRUMP: IRAN WILL PAY 'MANY TIMES OVER'
"Everyone is requested to comply with the security and safety instructions issued by the relevant authorities," the army added.
Meanwhile, Bahrain's Interior Ministry urged citizens and residents to remain calm, move to the nearest safe location and follow updates through official channels, according to a Wednesday post on X.
The ministry did not specify the nature of the threat.
Fox News Chief Foreign Correspondent, Trey Yingst also confirmed that Iranian drones had been launched targeting Kuwait.
Earlier, American fighter aircraft had carried out a self-defense airstrike on an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) missile launch site on Qeshm Island, Iran , on Tuesday, two military officials confirmed to Fox News.
"Earlier today, U.S. fighter aircraft used precision munitions to strike an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) missile launch site on Qeshm Island in self-defense.
"The strike was in response to IRGC aggression targeting U.S. personnel and assets. U.S. Central Command remains highly vigilant and fully postured to protect Americans across the region," an official said in a statement.
The strikes came hours after Tehran claimed it targeted a U.S. radar system at the Sheikh Isa base in Bahrain .
IRAN’S DRONE HUNT ESCALATES AS TEHRAN TARGETS US SPY TECH TO EXPOSE BATTLEFIELD SECRETS
Commercial vessels are seen anchored between Iran's Qeshm and Larak islands amid disruptions to maritime traffic in the Strait of Hormuz, Iran. (Fatemeh Bahrami/Anadolu via Getty Images, File)
In a statement, the IRGC claimed its operation was in response to violations of Iran's airspace by U.S. drones and said the action was taken to counter "hostile U.S. movements in the region," according to the semi-official, state-sponsored Mehr News Agency .
CENTCOM said later the Iranian attack drones were all intercepted.
"Multiple Iranian one-way attack drones launched by the IRGC today towards Bahrain were intercepted without any damage to U.S. equipment or injury to American personnel," the command said in a post shared on X .
Qatar also went on to condemn Iran's ongoing attacks on Bahrain on Tuesday, calling them a violation of Bahraini sovereignty.
"The Ministry underscores that the continuation of these attacks constitutes a grave escalation that threatens regional security and stability and undermines diplomatic efforts aimed at easing tensions," it said in a statement on X.

Qatar also described the Iranian attacks as a "flagrant" violation of international law and the principles of good neighborliness, warning that their continuation marked a serious escalation and undermined diplomatic efforts to defuse regional tensions.
The latest attacks also followed a wave of Iranian aerial strikes repelled by Bahrain on Sunday, during which the IRGC claimed to have targeted a radar system at the Al-Riffa helicopter base with another six drones.

The European Commission has proposed a new €45 billion ( approximately £37.5 billion) loan to help Ukraine as Russia intensifies attacks on critical infrastructure.
Ukraine anticipates a €70 billion (£58.3 billion) funding gap for 2027 as the war nears its fifth year.
Ursula von der Leyen , the bloc’s president, said Ukraine would only need to repay the loan after Russia had paid reparations for damage caused by the war.
The planned measure, which still needs approval from member states, would come on top of a similar loan of €90 billion (£75 billion) that was agreed by EU leaders at the end of 2026 to fund Ukraine.
Von der Leyen told reporters in Brussels that Europe “stands united” amid Russia’s war of aggression, reiterating the bloc’s support for Ukraine “in war and in peace”.
She added that Kyiv 's other international partners will be expected to provide the rest of the money to fill next year's funding gap.
The Commission proposes that up to €25 billion (£20.8 billion) of the new loan could be spent on military aid while the remaining €20 billion (£16.6 billion) has been earmarked on general budget support.
To finance the loan, the Commission will borrow on behalf of the EU on international markets, officials said.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy welcomed ⁠the proposal, saying the loan would "cover a significant part" of the country's budget and defence needs for next year.
"We very much hope for the swift adoption of this decision by the European Parliament and the Council (of EU governments) and count on the support of all EU member states," he said on X (formerly Twitter).
European Economy Commissioner Valdis Dombrovskis said Ukraine needed additional support because Russia is intensifying attacks on critical infrastructure and disrupting trade, particularly by blocking Black ‌Sea export routes.
"For almost five years, Ukraine has stood guard against the Russian aggression that also threatens our citizens, our territory, and our way of life,” he said. “Our support gives Ukraine a crucial strategic partner.”
Von ⁠der Leyen said she was confident all EU members would back the new loan, ⁠even though three — Hungary, the Czech Republic and Slovakia — opted out of the last one.
She said even EU countries that did not favour giving military aid to Ukraine were still committed to supporting Kyiv more generally, so their support for the loan could be attributed to meeting civilian needs.

articles.title_orig: Hims & Hers launches new peptide treatments — while admitting there's more to learn about efficacy
articles.title_zh: Hims & Hers launches new peptide treatments — while admitting there's more to learn about efficacy
articles.content_orig:
Hims & Hers Health on Wednesday said it will offer five formulations of peptides and longevity treatments compounded in the U.S. as part of the initial rollout of its Peptides+ platform, all of which are not approved by regulators.
Even as it announced the new products, Hims & Hers acknowledged it has more to learn about how best to use the peptides and how effective they are — underscoring the uncertainty surrounding the growing space.
The new offerings come after the federal government eased restrictions on compounding certain unapproved peptides, which are short chains of amino ​acids. Those products have exploded in popularity among fitness and longevity enthusiasts who attest that they help with muscle growth, rapid injury recovery and anti-aging, even though most lack evidence from robust human trials.
Hims in late October launched an early access list for the upcoming peptide offerings, and more than 10,000 people signed up within 15 days, a company spokesperson said in a statement.
None of the company's specific compounded products are approved by the Food and Drug Administration. But Hims said they are authorized by law and formulated by pharmacies "that adhere to rigorous quality standards and are licensed and inspected by state boards of pharmacy."
The products include compounded formulations of sermorelin, a peptide that stimulates growth-hormone release and is marketed for recovery, body composition and anti-aging; glutathione, a peptide promoted ‌for anti-aging and athletic recovery; and nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide, or NAD+, a coenzyme that plays a role in cellular metabolism.
The company will also offer compounded versions of vitamin B-12, a vitamin needed to make red blood cells, build DNA, and maintain healthy nerve function, and L-carnitine, an amino acid derivative that helps the body turn fat into energy. The FDA has approved certain prescription forms of both peptides for established medical uses, primarily for diagnosed deficiencies in those compounds.
Hims said it plans to add more peptides and therapies made in the U.S. over time. That includes BPC-157, an unapproved peptide derived from a protein found in human gastric juice that is marketed for healing processes. The company also aims to introduce another unapproved peptide called TB-500, which is derived from a naturally occurring protein in the body and is marketed for broader, systemic soft-tissue recovery and flexibility. Most of the research on both has been conducted in animals, not humans.
To receive the products, members on the Hims platform will start with an assessment of health history and goals with a licensed provider trained in peptide therapies, who can tailor a personalized plan to their needs, if appropriate.
The company said it intends to use its communication platform to check in with patients and ensure they are seeing desired results.
"If they're not, we need to do something about it," Dr. Anant Vinjamoori, Hims chief medical officer, told CNBC. "We need to, you know, adjust the dose when that's appropriate, or in some cases consider other compounds that's maybe a better fit. And of course, there will also be cases when we need to refer people to other care options."
However, Vinjamoori said there's still uncertainty over how to best use the peptides.
"We don't have all of this data that we're used to having with compounds like this," he said. "We have the opportunity to get it right, and I think we see that as our responsibility with a company of our size, our skill, and resources to really lead."
Vinjamoori added that people who have serious illnesses, such as cardiovascular disease, liver disease and kidney disease, will not be candidates for the compounds for now.
Meanwhile, Andrew Huberman, a well known neuroscientist, podcaster and Stanford University School of Medicine professor who recently joined Hims' board of directors, in a statement called compounds "real medical treatments, not just a wellness trend." He said Hims provides safe access through "trusted sourcing and physician oversight."
But health experts raised concerns about the broader mainstream marketing of peptides in the U.S. and accessing them on telehealth platforms.
"With peptides, I think you have to view them the same way you would view any drug that hasn't been rigorously tested," said Joshua Kritzer, a chemistry professor at Tufts University. "Without actual testing, all you have is anecdotal information, and that's just not enough information to put a substance in your body."
Kritzer said the lack of large clinical trials means researchers can't rule out potentially serious, rare complications from peptides — the kinds of risks that have led regulators to reject or pull otherwise effective drugs from the market after they underwent comprehensive testing in humans.
Without that testing, it's also unclear how telehealth firms, physicians and pharmacies can make decisions about what doses patients should take, said Paul Knoepfler, a cell biology and human anatomy professor at UC Davis Health. While some people rely on anecdotal data from real peptide users, "the dosing for these products really has not been established," he added.
Knoepfler said one risk is that injecting too much of a synthetic peptide into patients could trigger "weird immune responses that are really bad for one's health" because the body might recognize it as foreign.
"With the peptides, it's very loosey-goosey," Knoepfler told CNBC. "How does one even know what would be the effective amount for whatever you're hoping it will do, and what amount would have more risks?"
But he said the more contact patients can have with physicians around taking a compounded peptide, the better. Providers, including those tied to telehealth firms, should make sure patients are well-informed about the possible risks and unknowns of a given product and consider their preexisting conditions, cancer history and other medications, Knoepfler said.
That appears to be consistent with the approach Hims & Hers is taking. The company says patients who use the peptide and longevity products can also use its Care+ offering, which pairs treatment with ongoing support. That includes twice-a-year lab testing to track their progress and the ability to message providers trained in peptide therapy around the clock with any questions.
Still, Kritzer argued that having a doctor who only knows a patient from online, essentially mail-order platforms or websites "is not enough supervision to put you on a prescription medication," especially an unapproved one.
Hims' ability to legally sell some of these peptides stems from a major shift in federal oversight by the Health and Human Services Department. It issued a policy in October that says the Food and Drug Administration will not take enforcement action against licensed pharmacies, federal facilities or physicians that compound and dispense six unapproved peptides while formal rules are reviewed.
In practice, that means these pharmacies and other firms can now offer them, even though the peptides aren't yet on the FDA's official list of ingredients compounding pharmacies are allowed to make. It does not translate to formal approval of the specific peptides.
The policy followed a 2023 decision by the Biden administration where the FDA restricted compounding pharmacies from producing popular peptide formulations due to safety, impurity and immune-reaction concerns.
HHS Secretary ​Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has supported broader access to peptides, calling himself a "big fan" of the treatments and arguing that restrictions were driving Americans to potentially unsafe products from overseas. Kennedy has previously described using BPC-157 to treat a muscle injury.
The announcement also comes after Hims in February 2025 acquired a California-based peptide manufacturing facility equipped with advanced peptide synthesizers.

articles.title_zh: Hospitals Rush to Patch Java Vulnerabilities
articles.content_orig:
On November 17, 2026, the security research company Calif disclosed Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938) , a memory-corruption vulnerability in the Base64 decoder of OpenJDK, the most widely used Java runtime. Under the Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) 4.0, it scores 9.2 out of 10 (Critical). The flaw affects Java. OpenJDK published a security advisory and Oracle released patched builds in its November 2026 Critical Patch Update the same day, at 21:00 UTC.
The vulnerability lets a remote attacker with no credentials send malformed Base64 data to a Java application and overwrite memory next to the decoded output. Calif turned that overwrite into a leak of heap memory, similar to Heartbleed , and into remote code execution. Calif demonstrated pre-authentication remote code execution against Keycloak, Atlassian Jira, Atlassian Confluence, JFrog Artifactory, Jenkins and PingFederate in their default configurations, and post-authentication remote code execution against Apache Kafka, Apache Solr, Elasticsearch, Gerrit, and Spinnaker.
Cloudflare has released a new set of rules in the Cloudflare Managed Ruleset designed to detect malformed Base64 input patterns associated with this vulnerability. The rules are available on Pro, Business and Enterprise plans and are enabled by default with the Log action because malformed input and some benign application-specific token formats can resemble exploitation attempts. Blocking by default could therefore disrupt legitimate traffic. Customers can review matching requests in Security Events now and change the rules action to Block once they confirm it does not affect legitimate traffic.Â
The WAF is an additional layer of defense, not a replacement for the patch. Java4Shell can be reached through paths a WAF does not see, like outbound TLS responses, and the only complete fix is to update the Java runtime. Our analysts continue to monitor attack activity and will update the rules as new techniques and variations appear. You can track rule changes in the WAF changelog and get more information on how the vulnerability develops on the dedicated Cloudflare Zero Wire briefing .
We have seen no indication so far that Java4Shell was exploited on Cloudflare infrastructure.
Base64 is a common way to represent binary data as text. Java applications decode Base64 when they process authentication headers, tokens, file uploads and many network messages. To decode it faster, OpenJDK replaces frequently used code with specialized machine code, called intrinsics. On supported x86-64 processors, the Base64 intrinsic uses AVX-512 instructions to process 64 bytes at a time.
The bug sits in the handwritten assembly that handles the final characters of the input. When the tail of the input contains padding characters (=) in a position where valid Base64 never places them, the routine calculates a negative output length. That invalid length turns into a full 64-byte write. For a 65-character input, made of 64 characters followed by a single =, OpenJDK allocates a 50-byte output array and then writes 62 bytes past its end.
Java eventually rejects the input as invalid and throws an exception. By then, the neighboring memory has already been overwritten. An application's own input validation does not help, because the corruption happens inside the decoder before the application can reject the data.
The simplest trigger is 64 A characters followed by =. On OpenJDK 17, the trigger needs 128 characters followed by =, because the threshold for the fast code path is higher.
Exploitation is not point-and-shoot. The overwritten bytes are mostly fixed values, and the attacker controls only where the write lands. To build a working exploit, Calif arranged the Java heap so that the overflow enlarged neighboring arrays, which gave them first a way to read heap memory and then a way to write chosen bytes. Each target application requires its own exploit chain. Calif reported developing its first working local exploit in about three hours with the help of AI agents, so we expect other attackers to build exploit chains quickly.
Java4Shell affects a system only when all the following conditions are true:
OpenJDK 17.0.6 or newer, including distributions built from OpenJDK: Amazon Corretto, Eclipse Temurin, Microsoft Build of OpenJDK, Azul Zulu, BellSoft Liberica, SAP SapMachine, Red Hat OpenJDK, Oracle OpenJDK, Oracle Java SE and Oracle GraalVM for JDK. Check Oracle's advisory for the exact list of affected Oracle builds.
x86-64 with AVX-512 VBMI support, such as Intel Xeon Ice Lake, Sapphire Rapids, Emerald Rapids and Granite Rapids, or AMD EPYC and Ryzen Zen 4 or newer. ARM64 processors are not affected.
The application decodes attacker-controlled Base64 data with the standard Java decoder.
Many applications bundle their own Java runtime, and container images ship with a fixed Java Development Kit (JDK). Upgrading the system Java package does not update those copies, and it does not replace a Java virtual machine (JVM) that is already running. Every updated service needs a restart.
If you cannot update immediately, Calif documents two JVM startup flags that remove the vulnerable code path:
Both flags require a restart and may reduce performance for workloads that decode large amounts of Base64. They buy time while you patch. They do not replace the update.
Patching every Java runtime takes time, especially when JDKs are bundled inside applications and container images. Cloudflare WAF can reduce your exposure while you patch. A new managed rule, available on paid plans and enabled in Log mode by default, detects the malformed Base64 input that triggers Java4Shell. For Business and Enterprise customers, WAF attack score adds a machine learning layer that scores each request for remote code execution payloads, which helps catch variations and bypass attempts that signature-based rules can miss.

The rule is enabled by default with the Log action, because blocking by default could cause false positives on legitimate Base64 traffic. To review its matches, go to Security > Security Analytics > Events and filter by the rule ID. articles.title_zh: Leaker claims Apple developing four models of 20th anniversary iPhone
articles.content_orig:
Leaker Ice Universe says Apple is currently developing four models of the 20th anniversary iPhone which we’ve been referring to as the iPhone 20 . We’re expecting next year’s flagship models to be a radical new design with an all-glass appearance.
Why four models rather than two is unclear, but it seems possible Apple is testing two versions of both the Pro and the Pro Max to determine just how ambitious it can be with the final product …
Ice Universe says that two of the four models have quad-curved glass backs and two have flat glass. They indicate that Apple has already had to ramp back its ambitions with the curvature.
Apple is currently developing four models in total: two with flat glass backs and two with quad-curved glass backs. Apple has been prototyping this quad-curved design for three years, making several revisions along the way—particularly regarding the glass curvature, which is still being refined. The earliest version had a very pronounced curve; it was later reduced somewhat.
It’s standard practice for Apple to develop multiple competing prototypes of new devices, evaluating them for everything from usability and durability to ease of manufacturing.
We’re expecting Apple to use a combination of ultra-thin bezels and curved glass to create the illusion of no bezels at all – a more sophisticated version of the effect seen on the Apple Watch. Today’s report says the bezels are around 1mm thick.
The curved edges on the quad-curved version are approximately 1mm wide. However, because the glass curves around all sides, when viewed straight on from the front, the bezel becomes nearly invisible, creating a near‑borderless appearance. The actual visual effect could be quite stunning.
We yesterday saw an AI-generated render of what the design could look like. It’s expected to be the biggest redesign of the standard iPhone since the iPhone X.

articles.title_orig: The Fed's AI Bank Run Nightmare Is Suddenly Coming True
articles.title_zh: The Fed's AI Bank Run Nightmare Is Suddenly Coming True
articles.content_orig:
Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller on Wednesday called for aggressive action against inflation , saying the central bank needs to "shock people" as prices continue to rise more than he expected.
In the near term, the policymaker told CNBC in a live interview that a half percentage point increase in the Fed's benchmark rate is probably necessary at the Dec. 8-9 meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee.
He said the central bank needs to reverse the three quarter-point reductions from last year and may need to do more.
"I'm very, very concerned about inflation. It's kind of headed in the wrong direction, and it's spreading out," Waller told CNBC's Steve Liesman during a " Squawk Box " interview. "If you really want to get it down, you've got to start taking more aggressive actions."
"You might need to, like, shock people," he said.
Futures prices are fully pricing in a quarter percentage point hike at the FOMC's December meeting. They also are anticipating another move in January, followed by at least one additional increase before the end of 2027, according to the CME Group's FedWatch gauge.
Waller said the Fed wouldn't necessarily have to approve a half-point hike in December if it raised rates by a quarter point and signaled another move coming in January. However, Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh has been against that kind of forward guidance on grounds that it ties policymakers' hands.
"If you're not going to signal this very clearly to markets, you're going in January, my view is then you have to go 50 [basis points] in December to put it in place and get it done," he said.
Recent statements from other central bankers indicate a range of opinions , though most agree that more policy tightening is needed to bring down inflation.
In a speech Tuesday, St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem suggested as many as four hikes by the spring of 2027. Some Fed officials, including regional Presidents Beth Hammack of Cleveland and Lorie Logan of Dallas, have endorsed more gradual tightening.
However, continued inflation above the Fed's 2% target might push officials into a more aggressive stance.
The FOMC approved its first interest rate hike in more than three years in September, and then held rates steady at its October meeting. While inflation has continued to run hot since then, other Fed officials seem less eager to drop the policy hammer as heavily as Waller.
"I don't think the situation calls for dramatic action," New York Fed President John Williams said Tuesday in a conversation with Axios. "I think what we've been doing over the last past few months is ... working well. We're collecting the data, analyzing it, having the debate and making a decision."
The Fed in 2025 approved three rate cuts amid worries over the labor market and the belief that inflation would continue to moderate toward the central bank's 2% goal.
However, inflation reignited earlier this year after the strikes the U.S. and Israel launched against Iran in late February. Energy prices spiked while tariff impacts lingered, keeping most inflation readings above 3% .
"First of all, you've got to take back the three insurance cuts we put in last year," Waller said. "If the policy rate last summer in 2025 wasn't bringing inflation down, getting back to that isn't going to bring it down. So we may have to go above ... three hikes plus maybe some more to get it to start actually coming back down."
The FOMC later Wednesday will release minutes from the October meeting.

articles.title_orig: Kuwait says it repelled first Iranian attack in two months after US strikes island
articles.title_zh: Kuwait says it repelled first Iranian attack in two months after US strikes island
articles.content_orig:
Kuwait and Bahrain have said they repelled Iranian air attacks overnight as hostilities between Iran and the United States rise.
The drone attack on Kuwait was the first in more than two months. The Iranian army said it had targeted the Ali Al Salem Airbase, which hosts US forces, but Kuwaiti authorities did not report any damage.
It came after US warplanes struck an Iranian missile launch site on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, according to US military officials.
Meanwhile, the United Arab Emirates' state oil firm said a crew member was missing after one of its tankers was attacked in the Gulf waterway on Tuesday.
The recent exchanges of fire, as well as deadlock in negotiations on a peace deal, have raised fears of a major escalation in the nine-month-old war.
The conflict began when the US and Israel attacked Iran in late February.
Since then, Iran has retaliated for US and Israeli strikes by launching missiles and drones at Israel and Gulf Arab states hosting US military assets and personnel.
It has also attacked dozens of commercial vessels in and around the Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of global oil and gas shipments usually pass.
On Tuesday night, Kuwait's military said its air defences engaged "drone threats" but did not report any casualties or damage.
The Kuwaiti foreign ministry condemned the attack, saying it "flagrantly violated Kuwait's sovereignty, directly threatened its security and stability, and constituted a grave breach of international law".
"The explosions seemed to be coming from far away, but hearing them again after a period of calm was both surprising and worrying," Hani Mohammed, an Egyptian resident of Kuwait, told AFP news agency.
Bahrain's military also said on Wednesday that its air defence systems had "intercepted and destroyed several Iranian aerial attacks".
The island kingdom, which hosts the US Navy's 5th Fleet, has reported four attacks over the past six days, following a two-month lull.
Qatar, which has mediated in the stalled indirect talks between Iran and the US, said the Iranian attacks on its neighbours were a "dangerous escalation that threatens to complicate efforts aimed at containing tensions".
The Iranian army said its drones had targeted US Patriot air defence systems and drone and missile launch platforms at Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait.
Later, the army's commander-in-chief, Maj Gen Amir Hatami, warned the US and its allies that it would respond more forcefully to any new attacks on Iran.
"If the enemy repeats its mistake... we have the readiness and the plans to confront it and its supporters in a stronger, more crushing way and without geographic limitations," he said.
On Tuesday night, US fighter jets targeted a missile launch site on Qeshm Island "with precision munitions" in response to Iranian "aggression targeting US personnel and assets", US military officials said.
Iranian media reported explosions on the island but cited a local official as saying they had caused no damage to infrastructure.
In a separate development, the Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (Adnoc) said a search-and-rescue operation was under way for a missing sailor following an attack on one of its vessels in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday. The rest of the crew were safely evacuated and 11 were receiving medical care, it added.
The UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) centre reported that a tanker was struck by an unknown projectile about 13 nautical miles (24km) north of Khasab, in Oman's Musandam peninsula. It said the attack caused a fire on board that was extinguished.
Iran said two oil tankers and a ship carrying liquefied natural gas (LNG) had caught fire after hitting naval mines while sailing along an "authorised route".
At least 25 seafarers have been killed across the Middle East since the start of the war, when the Strait of Hormuz was effectively closed due to Iranian missile and drone attacks on commercial vessels and a US naval blockade of Iranian ports.
The US and Iran reached a preliminary agreement to end the conflict and reopen the strait in June, but it collapsed within weeks after Iranian attacks on shipping resumed and the US reinstated its blockade.
Iran insisted it would not give up some measure of control over the waterway and began targeting vessels using a southern route through Omani waters that avoids its preferred route through Iranian waters.
In recent months, the US military has been providing protection for tankers shuttling through the Strait of Hormuz, allowing crude oil exports from Gulf states to reach around 80% of pre-war levels, according to analysts.

articles.title_orig: Waymo suspends all driverless taxi rides on freeways after ban in California
articles.title_zh: Waymo suspends all driverless taxi rides on freeways after ban in California
articles.content_orig:
Waymo has temporarily stopped offering driverless taxi rides on freeways after California banned the vehicles from state freeways following recent traffic incidents.
The company had allowed riders to hail its robotaxis for freeway rides in the San Francisco Bay Area, Los Angeles, Phoenix, Miami and Austin. The California-based company offers rides on city streets in many other areas including Las Vegas, Dallas and Denver.
A Waymo spokesperson wrote in an email that the company has “temporarily restricted commercial freeway rides in all markets where we operate that service,” though it’s “continuing freeway testing with trained autonomous specialists behind the wheel.” The suspension was implemented last Wednesday, according to the spokesperson, but they didn't say how long it would last.
Related video: Why are gas prices dropping and how low will they go?
The suspension came after the California Department of Motor Vehicles banned the company's robotaxis from freeways that same day. The ban followed two incidents including one in which three Waymo driverless vehicles drove into a construction zone, DMV spokesperson Jonathan Groveman said in a statement.
The construction zone incident occurred on Nov. 5 and the second incident, which involved California Highway Patrol vehicles, occurred the next day on a highway in San Francisco, according to Groveman.
Video of the Nov. 6 incident circulated widely on social media last week. In the footage, a Waymo vehicle can be seen trying to bypass California Highway Patrol vehicles conducting a traffic break.
“The Department determined that Waymo’s driverless freeway operations pose an imminent hazard to public safety due to recurring incursions by its vehicles into active construction zones where construction workers, vehicles and equipment are present,” Groveman said.
Groveman added that “similar incidents” previously occurred on May 18.
The Waymo spokesperson said the “recent freeway construction zone encounters on U.S. 101 in California” did not “involve any injuries or collisions.”
California's restrictions bar Waymo from operating and testing its driverless vehicles on California freeways, according to Groveman. He said the restrictions will remain in effect until “Waymo demonstrates to the Department that it has taken effective corrective actions to address the deficiencies that precipitated the restrictions.”
Kelety reported from Phoenix.

articles.title_orig: In Choosing Shenzhen for Trump-Putin Summit, Xi Shows Off His Tech Ambitions
articles.title_zh: In Choosing Shenzhen for Trump-Putin Summit, Xi Shows Off His Tech Ambitions
articles.content_orig:
Host city offers showcase of China’s rise into a confident and innovative power central to global economy
I n a Shenzhen square on a balmy evening, locals and tourists watched the dozens of glinting towers that make up the city’s skyline ripple through the colour spectrum – cyan and violet, cyber green, China’s national scarlet and gold – repeatedly flashing the words “Apec 2026”.
The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit is a dream showcase for one of China’s most advanced cities, and the country’s leader, Xi Jinping , is basking in its neon glow.
On the sidelines, a series of high-profile bilateral meetings and the announcement of a historic three-way summit with Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin have cemented Xi’s status as an agenda setter on the global stage.
The broader Apec summit , meanwhile, provides an opportunity for China to present itself as a steward of multilateralism against what it terms “unilateralism and protectionism” – that is to say, trade measures taken against Beijing by countries such as the US.
All this is set against the futuristic backdrop that is Shenzhen, a city that perhaps better than no other embodies China’s rise into a confident, technologically innovative power central to the global economy.
A photo display in the Apec media centre charts Shenzhen’s transformation from sparsely populated marshland, calling it “a miracle in the history of world development created by the Chinese people”.
“[Xi] wants people to go home Chinamaxxing,” said Prof Astrid Nordin, of King’s College London. “Shenzhen is itself part of the message. It’s a showcase of Chinese technological and economic achievements, and of China’s claim that it offers opportunities for prosperity in a world increasingly characterised by uncertainty and conflict.”
Like the light show, the summit is being carefully coordinated. The Financial Times cited people familiar with the matter as saying it would be one of the most tightly controlled in the organisation’s history, with leaders having to travel to a state guesthouse beside Shenzhen’s tiger safari park to meet Xi. The paper said diplomats had grumbled that the format “seems designed to reduce the free-flowing discussion characteristic of prior editions”.
Setting out its expectations for the summit, China’s foreign ministry has said it looks forward to “practical results in key areas such as trade, connectivity, digital economy, AI and so on”.
Already, Xi has announced trade wins with Canada’s Mark Carney, extending remission measures for certain Chinese steel and aluminium products by two years in exchange for tariff relief on Canadian pork, fish and seafood exports.
A meeting with Papua New ⁠Guinea’s leader, meanwhile, showed how Beijing’s geopolitical priorities have been absorbed and reflected by its allies, with James Marape recounting to Xi how he had closed Taiwan’s office in his country despite domestic challenges in doing so.
The most important meeting will be between Xi and Trump. The leaders of the world’s two superpowers are expected to tackle a broad range of issues including AI and trade. In a move that could strain the fragile tariff truce that the two leaders first agreed last year, the Trump administration said on Monday it would further restrict China’s access to advanced AI chips.
Christopher Adams, a senior adviser at the law firm Covington who was at the centre of trade negotiations with China for the Obama and first Trump administrations, said: “The trade truce may increasingly look like a ceasefire in a war where major combat operations remain on hold but skirmishes are escalating to the point where the line between peace and war is blurred.
“I don’t see pressure to announce a further extension of the trade truce in Shenzhen. If a significant extension is announced, that would be an upside surprise.”
China has not hesitated to leverage Apec’s multinational platform in service of its arguments. A commentary by the state news agency Xinhua on Tuesday said: “Amid deepening geopolitical rivalries and growing global divisions, [China’s hosting] sends a clear signal that great-power competition need not be a zero-sum game, and that one country’s development need not come at the expense of another.”
The chair of the Apec senior officials’ meeting, Chen Xu, said Beijing had made trade “openness” a key focus of its Apec year and looked forward to “achieving more practical outcomes on the trade front”.
The much anticipated trilateral summit with Trump and Putin, on the other hand, could prove largely symbolic. For Xi, “it provides the appearance of China shaping the world order as an equal to the United States,” said Dr Kevork Oskanian, an expert on Russia at the University of Exeter. “Agreement on substantial issues, which would, in any case, require extensive preparatory negotiations, is unlikely.”
For China’s ruling Communist party, the political pomp has another key purpose. Nordin said summits were “occasions for leaders to tell stories about the world, about their country’s place in it … and one of the most important audiences for those stories is at home.”
For the locals watching the skyscraper light show on Monday night, the symbolism was not lost. China’s export might had helped it become increasingly powerful on the world stage, said one local man, who did not give his name. “It’s so great that the summit will take place in Shenzhen,” he said. “I feel very proud.”

The Russian Embassy in the Netherlands on Wednesday posted a statement asking if the Netherlands had openly joined the conflict in Ukraine on Kyiv's side after a Dutch-based company said its missiles had been used by Ukraine in an attack on the Crimean Bridge.
Ukrainian drones and missiles destroyed the central road section of the bridge linking Russia and Crimea on Tuesday, inflicting a military and symbolic blow on President Vladimir Putin days before he is due to meet the leaders of China and the U.S.
Destinus, a Dutch-headquartered startup, said Tuesday that its missiles were the only foreign-made weapons used in the Ukrainian attack on the Crimean Bridge, a rare operational role for a Western manufacturer in one of Kyiv's most significant long-range strikes of the war.
"Moscow has been duly informed of the NL (Netherlands) involvement," the Russian embassy said in a statement on X above a statement from Destinus detailing its role in the bridge attack.
"The confession has been well noted. Is The Hague openly joining the conflict?," the embassy said.

articles.title_zh: Putin Arrives in Asia With a Show of Force: Nuclear Bombers
articles.content_orig:
The Ministry of National Defense yesterday said it detected two Russian military aircraft flying off the nation’s east coast, while Japan protested to Moscow after two aircraft believed to be Russian violated its airspace the same day.
The reports, probably about the same aircraft, come ahead of Russian President Vladimir Putin’s arrival in Shenzhen, China, for this week’s summit of APEC leaders.
After flying through airspace to the nation’s east, the Russian aircraft, whose type it did not identify, exited Taiwan’s air defense identification zone (ADIZ) south of Taitung County, the ministry said.
Photo: AFP / Japanese Ministry of Defense
The ministry used joint intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance to monitor the full course of the activity and “responded appropriately,” it said in a statement, without giving details.
Earlier yesterday, Tokyo lodged a strong protest with Moscow after two aircraft believed to be Russian violated its airspace off the island of Okinoshima in southwestern Fukuoka, Japanese Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara said.
“The violation of Japan’s airspace by Russian aircraft is a serious infringement of Japan’s sovereignty,” Kihara said, adding that the safety threat was completely unacceptable. “We lodged a strong protest with Russia and urged it to prevent a recurrence.”
Photo courtesy of the Japanese Ministry of Defense
The Japan Self-Defense Forces scrambled fighter aircraft and took necessary measures in response, such as issuing warnings and notifications, the Japanese Ministry of Defense said.
The suspected Russian aircraft were subsequently confirmed to have transited the Tsushima Strait, passed between Yonaguni Island and Taiwan, and proceeded into the Pacific Ocean, it added, also without identifying the aircraft type.
Yonaguni is the Japanese island closest to Taiwan, about 100km off its east coast.
A map issued by Japan’s defense ministry showed a flight path to Taiwan’s east, heading in a southerly direction, implying the aircraft were the ones Taiwan spotted later.
The last confirmed violation of Japan’s airspace by Russian aircraft was off Rebun Island off Hokkaido in September 2024, the Japanese ministry said.
In 2023, Taiwan spotted two Russian warships off its eastern coast and sent its own aircraft and ships to keep watch.
Although it was not the first time Russian or former Soviet military aircraft had entered Taiwan’s ADIZ, such flights have become much less frequent since the Cold War, said Chieh Chung (揭仲), an adjunct assistant professor in Tamkang University’s Graduate Institute of International Affairs and Strategic Studies.
Chieh cited a 2010 incident in which a Russian Tu-95 strategic bomber entered Taiwan’s northeastern ADIZ before turning toward Japan’s Ryukyu Islands after Taiwan’s military issued a radio warning.
The aircraft’s identity was confirmed several days later through intelligence exchanges with neighboring countries, he said.
During the Cold War, Soviet aircraft flying to Cam Ranh Bay in Vietnam occasionally entered Taiwan’s ADIZ to shorten their routes or conduct electronic reconnaissance, Chieh said.
Yesterday’s flight was noteworthy, as it came ahead of the two-day APEC meeting that starts today and a planned US-China-Russia leaders’ summit tomorrow, Chieh said.
Moscow would have known that Japan was likely to publicize the aircraft’s movements, he said.
Chieh urged the Ministry of National Defense to disclose more details, including flight paths and entry times, as Japan had done.
Taiwanese fighter jets were likely scrambled to monitor the aircraft and should have been able to identify their models and possibly obtain photographic evidence, he said.
Releasing such information would demonstrate the military’s ability to monitor developments around Taiwan, Chieh added.

articles.title_orig: Nvidia’s Kress faces a divided workforce as some employees push for Huang’s return
articles.title_zh: Nvidia’s Kress faces a divided workforce as some employees push for Huang’s return
articles.content_orig:
The day before Colette Kress led her first earnings call as Nvidia's interim CEO, she did not want to talk about her predecessor, Jensen Huang .
"This is a new era for Nvidia," she told employees in an internal meeting on Monday, according to a person present, who spoke on the condition of anonymity. When someone brought up Huang, Kress quickly changed the subject, according to the person.
On Wednesday, Kress is due to address the whole company at the first Nvidia all-hands meeting since the public chaos over Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy and other reported relationships. And while Kress will be tasked with filling the leadership vacuum created by Huang's departure, she is also expected to tamp down public calls to bring him back.
Huang himself weighed in with his first public statement Tuesday saying he would be "honored" to return to Nvidia.
The interim CEO, who has served as the company's CFO since 2013, must steady employees and convince customers and investors that Nvidia can execute on its ambitious targets without the man who made them. For those at the top, that has meant making clear that the company does not plan to bring Huang back.
"The board has determined that they will not reinstate Jensen," Kress said in an interview with CNBC's Jim Cramer on Tuesday. "We want to grow in terms of everything that we need to do with our employees, our customers, our shareholders, and that is where we are going to focus moving forward."
Harvey Jones, the newly appointed chair of Nvidia's board, echoed the sentiment on Tuesday's earnings call. "The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO," he said in opening remarks.
Nvidia declined to comment for this story.
Kress stressed on the earnings call that the company was focused on the workers who remain, who she said are "committed to doing their life's work at Nvidia." The company also reported better-than-expected earnings and seemed to calm investors' nerves , at least for the moment.
Some employees are telling a different story. Support for Huang's return is growing inside Nvidia, sources tell CNBC. An online petition circulating since the weekend has nearly 200,000 signatures, with more than 10,000 of them claiming to be current Nvidia employees. Nvidia currently has roughly 42,000 employees.
Outside Nvidia, Huang's reinstatement has been called for by at least two major investors and tech heavyweights such as Elon Musk , Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney. President Donald Trump said he "would not mind" seeing Huang return as CEO.
Several employees posted on X over the last few days, voicing support for Huang and calling for his return. One robotics engineer said the founder's departure led to his own decision to leave.
Another senior Nvidia employee, Nader Khalil, sent a letter to the company's board and top executives warning that failing to reinstate Huang could lead to a loss of "irreplaceable talent," according to The Wall Street Journal.
Huang was known for his deep day-to-day involvement in his company's operations, often responding directly to engineers and chiming in personally on technical projects.
Engineering employees, in particular, were "extremely devoted to him, almost like a demigod," according to a former Nvidia employee who was at the company for more than 15 years and spoke to CNBC on condition of anonymity.
Wednesday's all-hands is a standard meeting: Nvidia traditionally holds one on the morning after each quarterly earnings call, according to the former employee.
Still, the meeting will be unlike anything the company has experienced. Employees tell CNBC that they plan to share their grievances at the all-hands, though it's still unclear if they will be allowed to ask questions. Kress will need to direct attention toward the business and away from Huang's return.
Huang took time to address employee questions during previous post-earnings all-hands meetings, the former Nvidia employee told CNBC, adding that Kress will be "eager to demonstrate there's a new sheriff in town."
Kress ended Tuesday's earnings call with an upbeat message: "Our customers and our partners are with us. And employees are committed. We've got this."
Wednesday's all-hands meeting could determine if employees agree.
— CNBC's Lora Kolodny contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: Steve Rosenberg: Historic talks with Xi and Trump are a coup for Putin
articles.title_zh: Steve Rosenberg: Historic talks with Xi and Trump are a coup for Putin
articles.content_orig:
The meeting hasn't even happened yet.
But Thursday's mini summit of Vladimir Putin, Donald Trump and Xi Jinping already looks like a win for the Kremlin.
Think back to 2022. After Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine President Putin was an international pariah. Western leaders were determined to isolate him and his country over the war in Ukraine.
Fast forward to 2026: Vladimir Putin has secured an historic meeting in Shenzhen. For the first time in history, the leaders of China, Russia and the United States will sit down – just the three of them – for talks.
That puts Putin exactly where he wants to be: at the top table of global politics, rubbing shoulders with the leaders of the two great powers.
It allows him to boast that Western pressure on Russia has failed.
"We see such examples in the failed attempts to isolate our country, Russia, which has faced unprecedented sanctions pressure," Putin told a business forum of the Asia-Pacific Economic Co-operation organisation.
That was followed by a meeting with Xi Jinping.
But the Kremlin says the "showstopper" event in Shenzhen will be Putin's trilateral with Xi and Trump.
It allows him to play global statesman, even as the Russian military continues to pound Ukrainian towns and cities, and the Kremlin continues to reject the idea of an unconditional, comprehensive ceasefire.
One short meeting is unlikely to reshape the world. But it's the optics that are key. The picture. The photo-op. Three leaders, three big powers, discussing big issues.
In a way, Vladimir Putin will use this meeting to send a holiday postcard to the rest of the world. Instead of "Wish you were here", he'll sign it: "Look: I'm here."
But what of those who are not at the table?
Among European leaders, and especially in Ukraine, there is concern that the three-way meeting might produce more than just a pretty picture, though not in a good way for Kyiv.
Donald Trump has already said that in Shenzhen he wants to discuss his "favourite subject" - the war in Ukraine. The Kremlin would likely welcome an opportunity to argue its case to Trump and Xi without Ukrainian officials or European leaders in the room.
Last month Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky expressed concern that the Putin-Trump-Xi meeting might resemble the Yalta Conference of 1945. That is when the leaders of the Soviet Union, Britain and the United States – Joseph Stalin, Winston Churchill and Franklin D Roosevelt - met to re-organise post-World War 2 Europe.
"We really don't want this to turn into 'Yalta 2, 3, 4' with a redistribution of influence," said Zelensky.
It is unclear whether China would want the Ukraine war on the agenda in Shenzhen. In its official statements on the upcoming trilateral meeting, Beijing has talked more generally about the need to discuss "safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability".
In Shenzhen, Russia will make the most of the optics. But a diplomatic victory is not the same as a military one.
Nearly five years after President Putin launched his so-called "special military operation", Russia is still struggling to win its war on Ukraine.
Over this time, it has suffered huge losses on the battlefield.
And the Ukrainian strike on the road bridge linking Russia to the Crimean Peninsula – carried out on the eve of the summit - was a blow to Moscow's prestige. The attack severely damaged part of the multi-billion-dollar bridge built by Russia after it annexed Crimea from Ukraine.
The damage is not only a logistical headache for the Russian authorities.
It is a reminder that the Kremlin's "special operation" has not gone at all to plan.
The Shenzhen summit may give Vladimir Putin a big stage, and a bright spotlight.
It does not necessarily bring him closer to winning the war.

articles.title_orig: Stock futures rise as Nvidia gains on earnings beat and solid outlook: Live updates
articles.title_zh: Stock futures rise as Nvidia gains on earnings beat and solid outlook: Live updates
articles.content_orig:
Stock futures climbed Wednesday morning after the S&P 500 fell for a fourth straight day. Traders also weighed Nvidia 's better-than-expected earnings report.
Nasdaq-100 futures were up 1%, while S&P 500 futures added 0.58%. Dow Jones Industrial Average futures were up 0.32%.
Shares of Nvidia were almost 3% higher in premarket trade, after jumping 4% in extended trading after the company's profit and revenue in the third quarter beat analysts' estimates. The company also lifted its revenue guidance for the fiscal year ending January 2028, calling for 75% growth year over year.
"The fact that they gave guidance is huge," said Gene Munster, managing partner at Deepwater Asset Management, on CNBC's "Closing Bell: Overtime. " " That is a very bullish sign. I expect the stock to move higher based just on that alone."
Neocloud companies also rose in extended trading. CoreWeave advanced 8%, while Nebius Group gained 10%.
During the regular trading day, the Dow dropped 1.6%. The S&P 500 slipped 1% and notched its lowest closing level since July 29, while the Nasdaq Composite shed 0.7%. During the day, the tech-heavy index touched its lowest level since April.
Looking ahead, traders are awaiting building permits and housing starts data. The Federal Open Market Committee's minutes from its October meeting will also be out in the afternoon. Federal Reserve policymakers last month decided to keep the overnight funds rate in a range of 3.75% to 4%.
On the earnings front, Lowe's, Target and TJ Maxx-parent TJX Cos are slated to report Wednesday morning.
Later this week, investors are awaiting a blockbuster initial public offering from Anthropic. The AI giant's shares are expected to be priced above the current range between $70 and $78, multiple sources told CNBC's David Faber on Tuesday.
Across the Atlantic, stock markets were mixed on Wednesday, with the pan-European Stoxx 600 hovering just below the flatline in morning trade. The U.K.'s FTSE 100 was 0.34% down, with France's CAC 40 sliding almost 0.1%, but Germany's DAX advanced 0.15%.
Most Asian markets closed in positive territory after a choppy trading session. South Korea's Kospi led gains in the region as chip heavyweights gained ground, ending 1.99% higher at 5,067.44, while Japan's Nikkei 225 gained 0.28% to close at 59,024.28,
Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index was 0.87% lower in its final hour of trade, while the CSI 300 on mainland China advanced 0.18% to 3,983.77. Australia's S&P/ASX 200 slipped 0.69%, marking a fifth straight day of losses.
Richard Reyle, chief investment officer at New Jersey-based Questar Capital Partners, said in a note Wednesday that Nvidia is "uninvestable."
"Nvidia is the Jenga tower of the whole AI trade, and that is not a compliment," he said. "A week ago, we thought this was a pedestrian story about a CEO whose ego got the best of him. Then we found out there was no clear succession plan, and poor corporate governance, with no Chairman until this scandal came to light."
He added that Nvidia's delayed 10-Q was a "red flag, as it's out of character from its previous releases."
"We believe there are significant questions about where Nvidia has been selling its chips," Reyle said. "For investors who own the stock, this is an immediate sell in our view. We have never owned Nvidia and believe the stock has been and remains uninvestable."
Shares of Nvidia were up around 4% in pre-market trading on Wednesday.
"There's another company set to begin a spectacular run (Anthropic), and every moment spent worrying about Nvidia is time that could have been spent finding the next winner," Reyle added. "News flash: NVDA ain't it."
Nvidia stock was up nearly 4% in premarket trading on Wednesday after reporting another earnings beat , as the fallout from CEO Jensen Huang's resignation continues to unfold.
The chip giant's stock was 3.96% higher at 5.08 a.m. ET on Wednesday in pre-market trading.
Neoclouds were buoyed by the results. CoreWeave was up 6.2%, Nebius 8.1% and Iren 7.4%.
U.S.-listed semiconductor stocks rose in pre-market trading Wednesday, following Nvidia's earnings beat.
Ahead of the opening bell, Nvidia stock was trading 3.9% higher, with the iShares and VanEck semiconductor ETFs both adding around 2.8%.
Marvell Technology added 4.3%, Arm was up by 3.8% and Micron gained 3.6%. KLA Corporation and AMD also traded more than 3% higher.
President Donald Trump has landed in China for the APEC summit, where he is due to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in the first trilateral talks between the three leaders on Thursday.
The meeting — taking place in Shenzhen, a major tech hub — puts trade and technology in sharp focus. Markets will be watching for any sign of progress on U.S.-China trade tensions or restrictions on advanced AI chips.
Xi opened the summit by calling for fewer trade and investment barriers and closer cooperation on artificial intelligence.
Traders are also watching for any signal on Ukraine, sanctions and energy, and the conflict in the Middle East , which could shape expectations for Russian oil exports and the geopolitical risk premium.
Precious metals sold off Wednesday morning, with gold falling to its lowest level in over a year and silver also plunging to a 52-week low, as expectations of interest rate rises from the Federal Reserve next month drew investors away from non-interest bearing assets.
Gold futures fell 2.34% to $3,761.84, while spot gold was down 2.38% at $3,758%. Silver futures slipped 3.5% to $45.72, as spot silver shed 3.6% to reach $45.67.
Nannette Hechler-Fayd'herbe, Lombard Odier Group's chief investment officer for EMEA and head of investment strategy, sustainability and research, said she remained optimistic on gold over the next 12 months, but warned that investors may need to be patient.
Hechler-Fayd'herbe does not expect the Federal Reserve or other central banks to embark on a sustained series of interest-rate hikes. But with U.S. real yields moving back up to 2.9%, from 2.6% not long ago, conditions are not yet supportive of an immediate rally, she said.
"This of course is not an environment where gold can immediately perform, so a little bit of patience on gold I think is warranted," she told CNBC's "Squawk Box Europe" Wednesday.
European stock markets were largely negative in early trading on Wednesday, with the Stoxx 600 edging just below the flatline shortly after 8:00 a.m. in London (3:00 a.m. E.T.).
Technology stocks advanced 1.16%, leading continental sectors, while industrial goods added 0.19%. But most other sectors were in the red, with basic resources tumbling 2.41%, while autos fell 0.43%.
Germany's DAX was up almost 0.1% in early trading in Frankfurt.
The U.K.'s FTSE 100 was down 0.32% in London, while in Paris, the CAC 40 was flat.  In Milan, the Italian FTSE MIB was hovering just below the flatline.
Indonesia's central bank on Wednesday raised rates by 25 basis points in a surprise move, bringing its policy rate to 6% — last seen in December 2024.
Economists polled by Reuters had expected the bank to keep rates steady at 5.75%.
The Bank of Indonesia said the move was to strengthen the currency and a preemptive measure to keep inflation in its target range of 1.5% to 3.5%.
The Indonesian rupiah depreciated to a record low of 18,285 against the greenback on Tuesday, while the inflation rate in the country was at 3.23% in October.
Markets in Asia ended mostly higher on Wednesday in choppy trading as investors assessed Nvidia earnings, Japan exports data, and comments from global leaders at the APEC summit in China.
South Korea's Kospi led gains in the region as chip heavyweights rose, rising 2% to 5,067.44. The small-cap Kosdaq also advanced 2% to close at 662.81.

articles.content_orig:
President Trump said on Wednesday the United States had concluded a “very big trade deal” with the Philippines, but offered no details, while Manila said the two countries had reached only an understanding on economic cooperation.
“We’ve just consummated a very big trade deal, the biggest trade deal we’ve ever made so far, and it is a fair deal for both countries,” Trump told a state lunch event at the Philippine presidential palace.
“We were very happy with that, and we didn’t know that was going to take place, but it took place very quickly and it’s a magnificent deal for both.”
The Philippine president’s office later said both sides reached an understanding on areas of economic cooperation, but made no mention of a trade deal.
Trade representatives of both countries will work closely to translate the commitments into concrete initiatives, it said in a statement.
The deal with the Philippines would be great for US farmers and those in the energy business, Trump added on Truth Social, but gave no further details.
Negotiations on a trade deal between the two allies were not mentioned in any schedules released by either country.
There was no immediate comment from the office of Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr about the deal Trump was referring to.
“The US offered for us to diversify our food supply and energy requirements,” said Jose Manuel Romualdez, the Philippines’ ambassador to the United States.
Asked whether anything was signed, Romualdez said in a text message, “None.”
On Tuesday, Trump said Thailand would scrap all tariffs and substantial non-tariff barriers on its imports from the United States in a trade deal expected to be finalized in coming weeks.

articles.title_orig: Nvidia says no longer shipping 'Hopper' AI chips to China
articles.title_zh: Nvidia says no longer shipping 'Hopper' AI chips to China
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia warned its customers that new legislation on Chinese companies remotely accessing its artificial-intelligence chips could expose it and them to U.S. "legal action," sources told CNBC.
The chip giant is facing increasing scrutiny from U.S. lawmakers over Chinese companies' access to its advanced chips, which U.S. export controls restrict from going to China.
Nvidia messaged chip buyers in recent months to caution that the proposed Remote Access Security Act, or RASA, would give the U.S. government broader authority to control access to cloud services in the same way as physical hardware, potentially exposing both parties to legal risk, according to two people with direct knowledge of the matter. The people asked not to be named while discussing private communications.
It also said that, for now, it would not sell its chips to customers who rent more than 50% of the graphics processing units, or GPUs, to Chinese companies, the people said.
Separately, the Financial Times reported earlier this month that Nvidia verbally told data-center clients to direct at least 51% of their services to non-Chinese customers under future contracts.
Regulators have had limited powers to control companies' access to those chips through cloud services hosted overseas.
RASA passed the House of Representatives in January but has not yet passed the Senate. Remote access to the chips has provoked the ire of President Donald Trump 's administration, which has sought to keep the chips out of China to maintain the U.S. lead in the AI race.
CNBC reported on Nov. 5 that Chinese lab Moonshot AI sought access to Nvidia chips through data centers in Europe. The Trump administration previously singled the company out, accusing it in July of accessing the chips through centers in East Asia.
The U.S. Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security, or BIS, announced on Monday an interim final rule designed to prevent Chinese companies' remote access to AI chips.
Nvidia and BIS did not respond to a request for comment.
On Sunday, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called for a "dramatic shakeup" at Nvidia after Jensen Huang 's shock departure as CEO, amid reports of an extramarital affair with a woman U.S. authorities reportedly suspect of spying for China.
Bessent suggested other Nvidia executives should face scrutiny over the chip giant's compliance with export controls.
"I want to keep coming back to what was the culture at Nvidia, and were they pressing these seemingly illicit sales to goose their revenues and their earnings?" Bessent told Fox News.
In an August securities filing , Nvidia said it sought to "strictly comply with all applicable export control regulators" but did not have "physical control of our products after sale" and relied on its customers' and partners' compliance programs.
Huang has been asked to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 3.

articles.title_orig: Russia's energy crisis is so bad it's mass-importing fuel and looking to low-grade fuel for pump stations
articles.title_zh: Russia's energy crisis is so bad it's mass-importing fuel and looking to low-grade fuel for pump stations
articles.content_orig:
Ukraine's refinery strikes on Russia are pushing the world's second-biggest energy exporter to buy vast volumes of petrol from overseas and instruct officials to prioritize lower-quality fuel.
The crisis has been months in the making, as Kyiv wages a long-range strike campaign pummeling Russian energy facilities, claiming this week to have knocked out about 55% of total refinery capacity so far.
A new readout from a Russian government meeting on Tuesday signals how deep the Kremlin's fuel woes are growing.
Alexander Novak, a deputy prime minister and Russia's senior official overseeing energy, was cited telling his subordinates to prioritize expanding petrol imports and "securing additional volumes of out-of-class fuel."
The latter means that Moscow is now focusing on making lower-grade fuel available. It's traditionally held to a K5 rating, a quality standard its gas stations have maintained for 10 years.
Fuel below this rating was typically reserved for exports outside Russia's Eurasian trade bloc, as well as for niche uses such as the military, state reserves, or oilfields.
Meanwhile, local officials and media in at least six Russian regions announced gasoline rationing at some pump stations earlier this month, typically capping customers at 30 liters of petrol, or about 7.93 gallons, a day.
Reuters reported in August that similar restrictions had rolled out in Moscow areas among some chains, depending on the station type, with long queues forming outside some pumps near the capital.
Russia remains a net fuel exporter , shipping millions of tons of crude oil and other products like diesel abroad.
Add BI in Google so our reporting is easier to find when you’re searching for what matters.
But with its refineries under siege, it's struggled to turn enough of that crude into refined petrol for gas stations at home.
International organizations that track fuel shipments say Moscow has surged imports for those products over the last few months, mostly from Morocco, India, and Turkey.
While Russia's monthly fuel imports roughly maxed out at 5,000 metric tons of petrol products and additives from 2023 to 2025, it brought in over 416,000 metric tons of such goods by sea this August, according to the Center for Research on Energy and Clean Air.
The Helsinki-based non-profit said Russia further imported another 234,000 metric tons of seaborne oil products in September.
London-based shipping analytics firm Vortexa separately put Russia's August fuel imports at about 470,000 metric tons.
Meanwhile, Ukraine's military intelligence agency, GUR, said on Tuesday that Kyiv's attacks had forced Russia to import about 989,000 metric tons of fuel and high-octane additives by sea from July 18 to October 23.
Russia has also been importing fuel by rail, from countries like Belarus or Kazakhstan, though these aren't tracked as closely.
Reuters reported in July that Russia had imported about 453,000 metric tons in the first six months of 2026 over land, or about a 20-fold increase year-on-year.
The most recent time Russia shipped in fuel on those levels was in 2014, when it imported 1.6 million metric tons of motor gasoline amid a domestic supply squeeze.
Moscow had arranged a deal with Belarus to trade Russian crude oil for refined petrol it had previously sold to Minsk. The arrangement brought in another 808,000 metric tons in 2015.
But those imports took place over entire years, while GUR's estimate of nearly 1 million metric tons in imports covers just four months.
Novak, the senior Russian energy official, said in October that Russia was importing about 10% of its gasoline, though he did not provide any specific trade figures.
"We'll be importing at least until the end of the year," Novak told state media, adding that Russia also had to top up reserves depleted during the summer when gas ran short.
Novak's office and the Russian energy ministry did not immediately respond to comment requests sent outside regular business hours by Business Insider.

articles.title_orig: China’s Xi pitches free trade at APEC amid Trump’s global trade disruptions
articles.title_zh: China’s Xi pitches free trade at APEC amid Trump’s global trade disruptions
articles.content_orig:
China’s President Xi Jinping has urged support for “free and open trade”, pitching Beijing as a stable partner – as opposed to President Donald Trump-led Washington – and pledging to stand up to trade protectionism.
Speaking on the sidelines of the annual Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit on Wednesday in Shenzhen, southern China, Xi took aim at rising “unilateralism and protectionism”.
His remarks appeared to be a veiled criticism of Trump’s America First policies, under which the United States has imposed tariffs on both allies and economic rivals.
Xi is due to meet Trump, who is travelling from the Philippines for the APEC leaders’ summit later on Wednesday. Xi and Trump are then due to hold an unprecedented three-way summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
On the sidelines of the APEC summit, Xi told business executives that the Asia Pacific must pursue more open trade and equitable growth to remain stable and dynamic.
Trump’s America First approach of tariff hikes and other moves runs counter to APEC’s aim of eventually forming a Pacific Rim free trade zone.
Washington also limits Chinese access to leading-edge US technology, such as the Nvidia computer chips that help power artificial intelligence (AI).
“We must firmly uphold the rules-based multilateral trading system with the World Trade Organization at its core, support free and open trade and investment, maintain the stability and smooth operation of global industrial and supply chains,” Xi said.
He added that China sought to “provide a more stable, predictable and beneficial environment for global enterprises” and would continue to expand access in its manufacturing and services sectors.
“Starting by lowering tariffs, expanding access, and exploring regulations and management standards, China will conduct deep-seated reform,” Xi said.
“While pursuing its own development, China has shared opportunities with other countries and worked for common development,” he said. “It has steadily brought stability and predictability to world economic growth and international trade and economic cooperation.”
George Chen, partner and chair of digital practice at The Asia Group, told the Associated Press news agency that Xi’s speech highlighted China’s aim to lead global industrial transformation.
“While he didn’t say so explicitly, his message was clear: China wants to be seen as a partner in global technology development, in contrast to Washington’s more restrictive approach,” Chen said, noting that Xi did not mention export controls, Nvidia, or the US directly.
Xi’s message is “likely to resonate with many Global South countries, and reinforces Beijing’s effort to contrast its technology strategy with that of Washington”, Chen added.
